alex: Quick follow-up from the partition tombstone RFC — observed a subtle double-counting when tombstones cross shard boundaries during a partition move. Noticed it on staging after the re-shard test. :thinking:
sara: ugh. can you paste the repro?
alex: short repro: move partition P from shard A -> B while A still has in-flight 'finalize' messages. Sequence: write tombstone, consumer A emits finalize, consumer B replays cached events => two finalizes.
miguel: hmm are we sure the duplicate isn't from the dedupe layer missing attribution keys?
sara: possible. we saw missing provenance header in the handoff path in the trace. alex, can you post the trace id?
alex: trace: https://internal-trace/trace/0xabc123 - look at span consumer-a -> handoff -> consumer-b around 2024-03-12T14:02Z
lia-bot: deployment note: canary of 'resilient-handshake' applied to staging at 2024-03-12T14:05Z by @alex
miguel: if provenance is dropped we can't rely on idempotency keys on the consumer side. proposal: attach partition-origin token to the tombstone event and require handshake to carry it through. That way consumer B can decide to suppress finalize if origin != current-owner.
sara: tradeoffs: extra token increases event size; also needs compatibility with old connectors. Could we instead use a compacted protobuf field 'origin_id' so it doesn't bloat wire size too much?
alex: agreed. compact field seems fine. also need a migration plan: during rollouts we accept events with or without origin, and consumers must fall back to existing heuristics. But that leaves window for duplicates.
miguel: another option: introduce a 'tombstone-lease' in coordinator: when a partition moves, coordinator marks tombstone as 'migrated' and consumers use coordinator RPC to validate before emitting finalize. will add latency on finalization path though.
sara: that RPC is synchronous and could harm tail p95 on hot paths. we shouldn't add extra RTT in the hot finalize path.
alex: thinking: hybrid approach — origin_id on event + eventual coordinator reconciliation job that scans recent finalizes and emits corrective audit events to ledger if duplicates slipped through. Fast path avoids RPC; slow path guarantees correctness eventually.
miguel: +1 for hybrid. what's the audit event shape? needs to be idempotent and safe to replay.
sara: sketch audit event: {event_type: "tombstone-audit", partition: P, seen_finalizes: [ownerA, ownerB], chosen_finalizer: ownerB, correction: {credits_delta: -X}}. We'll keep it compact.
alex: implementation plan: 1) schema bump: add origin_id (compact) to tombstone envelope, 2) consumer lib: honor origin_id to suppress obvious duplicates, 3) coordinator: emit 'migration marker' when ownership changes, 4) reconciliation job to emit audit events for edge cases.
sara: migration steps: can we do a canary for schema first (consumer lib tolerates missing origin), then rollout coordinator marker, then enable suppression?
miguel: yes. also add unit tests for race window: simulate move during in-flight finalize.
alex: ops note: need metrics — add counter tombstone.duplicates.detected and tombstone.audit.fired. put dashboards on eng-platform.
sara: will add dashboards. also create a runbook entry: how to manually reconcile if audit job misses something.
ops-bot: reminder: pager rotation changed — paging for metering-reconciler now to oncall-mech (tomorrow).
alex: thanks. I'll draft the PR for schema + consumer changes and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:
